A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
‘leveling the playing field’ for analyses of single base resolution DNA methylomes is a critical first step in understanding the biological significance of cytosine methylation.

we propose that the ‘methylation level’ at a cytosine should be defined as the fraction of cytosines at that position that are methylated, with the denominator being the number of cytosines observed in the sequencing data.

the ‘methylation level’ of a cytosine or cytosine context is best described as a proportion of methylated reads, with the caveat that this proportion can be influenced by the sequencing depth, the bisulfite conversion efficiency, the sequencing error rate, and the number and quality of the input reads.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ‘leveling’ of DNA methylation data should be performed at the level of the cytosine and not the CpG site, and that the ‘level’ should be defined by the proportion of methylated cytosines in the population.

, when analyzing DNA methylomes, it is important to consider the following: 1) the type of methylation (i.e., 5-methylcytosine or 5-hydroxymethylcytosine), 2) the number of reads, 3) the number of cytosines in a region, 4) the type of cytosines, 5) the sequencing platform, and 6) the sequencing depth.

, for a given cytosine, methylation level is best estimated from the number of reads supporting the methylation state (i.e., the number of reads containing a C or T, respectively), as opposed to the proportion of reads supporting a given methylation state.
